title: Weekly AQI Exposure Hours
dataSources: Weather-station observations (`ecowitt:obs`, `weatherflow:obs`), air-quality readings (`purpleair:aqi`, `airgradient:sensor`), soil-moisture and greenhouse sensors (`plant:sensor`), aquarium controllers (`aquarium:sensor`).
app: Personal weather stations (Ecowitt/Ambient/Davis/WeatherFlow), air-quality sensors (PurpleAir/AirGradient), and aquarium/greenhouse/soil sensors via HEC and MQTT.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=purpleair:aqi
| eval poor_air=if(aqi>=100,1,0)
| bin _time span=1w
| stats sum(poor_air) as poor_samples by _time
| eval poor_hours=round(poor_samples/12,1)
| where poor_hours>6
| sort - poor_hours
description: Adds up how many hours each week your local air quality sat in the unhealthy range, useful for planning runs, ventilation, or filters.
value: One nasty hour is easy to shrug off; a weekly exposure total makes smoke and pollution episodes feel real enough to act on.
implementation: Forward AQI readings at a five-minute cadence; review weekly exposure totals and compare them against symptoms or outdoor plans.
visualization: Weekly bar chart of estimated unhealthy-air exposure hours.
grandmaExplanation: It highlights how many hours this week the air around your home was bad enough that you probably should have changed plans.
